# git: alias: add lock/unlock to temporarily disable push

Add `git lock` / `git unlock`, which forbid pushing to a remote for a while and restore it afterwards, without touching fetch. **Motivation:** freeze a branch during a long rebase or experiment, prevent an accidental publish, guard a shared mirror — and get the original state back without remembering the URL.

```bash
$ git lock          # disable push to origin; fetch/pull still work
$ git unlock        # restore push (pushurl falls back to the fetch url)
```

PoC: `git remote set-url --push origin no_push` to lock (a sentinel that shows up in `git remote -v`), `git config --unset remote.origin.pushurl` to unlock. The sentinel-plus-unset design is chosen because it is symmetric (the original state is "pushurl unset", so nothing is rewritten), self-documenting and detectable. Out of scope for the PoC: a remote argument, backing up a pre-existing custom `pushurl`, idempotency and status reporting.
